analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech is a niche pharma-cleanroom turnkey play riding India's pharma/biotech capex wave, with FY25 showing a breakout (revenue +55% to ₹150 Cr, PAT +117% to ₹13 Cr) on a small ₹270 Cr base. At P/E 27.6 against ~25% earnings growth, PEG ≈1.1 — reasonable but not the bargain I hunt for; I'd wait for another quarter of execution proof.
key_strengths: Niche dominator in pharma cleanrooms — 5Y PAT CAGR 26.6%, ROE 18%, ROCE 21%
Clean balance sheet: borrowings ₹10 Cr vs equity ₹95 Cr (D/E ~0.1); promoter holds 68.5%
Small ₹270 Cr cap + India pharma capex tailwind = genuine ten-bagger optionality
key_risks: Lumpy project revenues (89→70→114→125→97→150) — FY25 spike may not repeat
OCF only ₹3 Cr vs PAT ₹13 Cr — earnings quality weak, working-capital heavy
Recent listing with IPO proceeds (financing +₹24 Cr) — unproven public-market execution
red_flags: OCF/PAT divergence: ₹3 Cr OCF on ₹13 Cr PAT in FY25
5Y revenue CAGR only 11% despite 'expanding' label — growth is back-end loaded
analysis.detailed_analysis: The story here is simple and Lynch-friendly: a small promoter-led engineering firm (68.5% promoter holding, ₹270 Cr mcap) building cleanrooms for pharma/biotech — a sector I can see growing from my armchair given India's CDMO and vaccine capex boom. FY25 numbers are genuinely exciting: revenue up 55%, PAT up 117%, ROE 18%, ROCE 21%, and debt negligible. PEG at ~1.1 (P/E 27.6 / ~25% growth) is acceptable for a fast grower, and the ₹24 Cr equity raise gives them fuel for the ₹26 Cr of investing outflow in FY25.
